text: The Patriots' 45-17 demolition of the Raiders on Sunday was nothing short of dominant, with Drake Maye delivering what appears to be his best performance of the season—accounting for five total touchdowns and looking considerably more confident, particularly on deep balls, despite being without his top receiver and with both starting cornerbacks sidelined. Maye's film shows a marked improvement in decision-making and execution from the week prior, suggesting he's found a rhythm that was largely absent in the early going this season, even as the injury report got worse: RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and LT Will Campbell (knee) both departed Sunday's win, with Campbell believed to have suffered a knee sprain that sent ripples of concern through a team already dealing with multiple starters unavailable. That the Patriots could cruise to such a lopsided victory while hemorrhaging bodies up front and on the perimeter speaks volumes about both the roster's depth and Maye's emerging ability to navigate adversity, though the health situation heading into the next stretch figures to dominate conversation around New England.
